Our Belief01

A chandelier is the one fixture a room is built around — it deserves more thought than a dropdown menu on a lighting website.

So we still bend the brass, cut the crystal and wire the arms ourselves, in small runs, for people who notice the difference.

The Meadow — nine-arm chandelier
FEATURED PIECE

Nine arms, one continuous brushed-brass line.

Modelled after a climbing vine, each arm curves off a single spine and ends in a hand-blown dimpled globe — the kind of texture that throws light in every direction instead of one straight beam. Built for a living or dining ceiling with real height to fill.

  • FinishBrushed antique brass
  • Arms9, hand-formed
  • GlassDimpled amber globes, hand-blown
  • Fit forDouble-height ceilings, staircases
  • Lead time4–6 weeks, made to order
The Bhawan — cut-crystal table lamp
FEATURED PIECE

A quieter light, for a bedside or a console.

A deep-cut crystal urn on a cast brass foot, topped with a hand-loomed linen shade that lets the light through soft and warm rather than bright. Heavy enough to feel permanent; simple enough to sit next to anything.

  • BaseHand-cut crystal, cast brass foot
  • ShadeHand-loomed linen
  • Height26 in, base to finial
  • Fit forBedside, console, study
  • Lead time2–3 weeks, made to order
HOW IT'S MADE

Every piece passes through four pairs of hands before it ships.

i.

Brass, bent to form

Solid brass rod is heated and hand-bent over wooden formers to get the curve of each arm — no two batches come out perfectly identical, and that's kept on purpose.

ii.

Crystal, cut by eye

Glass blanks are scored and faceted by hand on a stone wheel, the way it's been done in the same workshops for generations.

iii.

Wired and tested

Every fixture is fully wired and burned in for 48 hours before it's approved to leave the workshop.

iv.

Finished by hand

Brass is hand-rubbed to its final patina — antique, brushed or polished — as the very last step before packing.

v.

Fitted to your ceiling

We ask for your ceiling height and drop before we build, so the chain or rod length arrives correct — not trimmed on site.

vi.

Packed to survive transit

Each arm and globe is individually wrapped and boxed in-house; nothing is boxed by a third-party courier.
